newsitem.title: USA: Two dead, other victims feared in wall collapse.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, other victims feared in wall collapse.

text.p: At least two people died and five were injured when a concrete wall collapsed on Thursday at a shopping centre renovation project, and rescue workers were digging for more victims, officials said.
Houston Fire Chief Eddie Corral told reporters that as many as six other people were feared dead under what he described as "several tons" of rubble.
"We're pretty certain there may be other people under the debris. We won't know until we get in there and start pulling off some of the debris," he said in a news conference.
Earlier a fire department spokesman said three were confirmed dead, but he scaled back the number for now.
Corral said the victims were thought to be "mall walkers," or elderly people who walk in the shopping mall for exercise.

The collapse occurred when demolition teams were tearing down a vacant department store to make way for a Magic Johnson movie theatre. The wall, 150 feet long and 20 feet tall (45 by 6 metres), enclosed a hallway next to the store.
One witness said the wall may have been knocked over by demolition equipment.
"They were picking at the building with one of their tractors and then the next thing you know the whole thing just came down," Nunez said. "It was like a row of dominos."
Mayor Bob Lanier, who toured the scene, said the city was investigating the cause of the collapse but it was too early to speculate on what had happened.

Officials said four of the five injured suffered only minor wounds, but that one victim was in surgery for serious leg injuries. Corral said a firefighter also had twisted his ankle during rescue operations.

Rescue teams went through the rubble with dogs and detection equipment searching for victims, but Corral warned that the process of finding others buried in the rubble would be slow because the debris was so heavy.
Bulldozers and cranes worked on the site clearing away slabs of concrete and large roof beams that lay propped up against the building after the collapse.
Former NBA star Johnson issued a statement from Los Angeles expressing his sympathies for the victims.
